main_body: Wooden rack frame holding five kegs (two upper, three lower) seen end-on against a dark grey back wall, with a brown top beam across the full width
top_band: rows 8-12 at x=16 are a brown gradient (L109, 130, 157) that reads as the front face of the top beam with a highlight at its lower edge. There is no separate lighter horizontal surface and no step to a front face. The keg ends and shelf edges below show no top surface either.
evidence: The whole piece is drawn straight on, like an architectural elevation. The top beam (rows 8-12) is a vertical face that gets lighter toward its bottom edge. It is not a foreshortened top, and it is the same wood family as the face below. The kegs are circular end-on discs with hoops and bungs, and no keg shows a top surface or curved stave top. The lower shelf is only a 1-row light line (row 21, L170 at x=23) and the base is a 1-2 row strip, so neither reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. The frame has no visible top faces on its beams or base, which the frame kind requires. This matches the red front-elevation case in the guide.

style.evidence: The wood ramp has about 5 steps (dark #6d3b15, mid #9a5435, #b77246, light #d59147, plus #9e684b), and the grey wall and metal hoops add 2-3 more. The outlines are tinted brown rather than neutral (only 6% of dark edge pixels are neutral). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the keg ends carry hoop, bung and stave variation. Median colours per tile is 13, against 17 and 20 for the references, so it is a little thinner. Its total of 13 distinct colours is well below the references' 38-40, and the grey wall is plain compared with the references' textured stone and cloth. Overall it sits acceptably next to the references, a bit simpler but not sticker-like.
